questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other drivers.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a person is blind or partially blind. You must always give them the right-of-way when they are crossing.

questions.question: Before driving, what should a driver taking an over-the-counter drug do?

options.text: Read the labels on the drug for warnings about driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug for warnings about driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your driving ability. Always read the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Hold the steering wheel tightly and take your foot off the accelerator. Apply the brakes lightly once the vehicle has slowed down. Do not move to the shoulder until the car slows considerably.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs usually look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road or on both sides of a divided highway.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink with a cold medicine might affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unsafe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unsafe to drive.
questions.explanation: Legal medications, both prescription and over-the-counter, can reduce your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve.
Drive at least 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. Speed advisory signs show the recommended speed for the upcoming road condition.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving over the speed limit or driving too fast for road conditions causes many accidents. Always drive at a safe speed within the legal limit and with traffic flow.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
A traffic light is ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass other vehicles. If there is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, drivers on the solid line side cannot pass. If both lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help the body get over the effects of alcohol. Nothing else speeds this up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic moves in both directions ahead.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts greatly improve your chances of surviving a crash and avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts during front-end crashes. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers and carefully move off the road. Park where other drivers can see you. Lift your hood so drivers know your vehicle has a problem.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to the car in front of you):

options.text: Can anger other drivers.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Stops other drivers from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and can make other drivers angry. It is considered aggressive driving and can result in a traffic ticket.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Let them get completely away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and keep your speed.
Speed up to get through the area faster.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross in front of you. When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead.
You may pass, but only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. Drivers must obey all regulatory signs. This sign means passing is not allowed in this area.
